title: One deep dive on a viral like counter: numbers, options, compare, pick, watch
captions: State the problem with a number. The counter lives in DynamoDB. We guess a viral post peaks at 20,000 likes per second. One partition takes at most 1,000 writes per second. One row cannot keep up.
Give two or three options. Keep one row, split the count across 50 rows, or add likes up in each app server and write once a second.
Compare on the needs you agreed. A is too slow. C can lose the last second or so of likes if a server crashes. Only B meets all three.
Pick, and say the cost. 50 shards cut each key to about 400 writes per second, well under the limit. The cost is reading 50 rows, so a small job sums them each second and pages read that one total.
Say what you would watch and what would change your mind. Track throttled writes and how stale the total gets. If counts had to be exact, you would choose again.
